---
title: "Updating the metadata on Zenodo"
description: |
  Use the `update` command to update metadata on an existing Zenodo deposit without changing its files or DOI.
order: 3
---

Imagine this:

> You have published a record on Zenodo but afterwards discovered a typo, need
> to correct information, or want to add missing metadata after publishing a
> deposit.

Instead of making a new record, you just want to update the metadata without
having to upload the files again or create a new DOI.

The `update` command updates the metadata of an existing Zenodo deposit based on
the `.zenodo.toml` file.

Unlike the publish command, update only changes the metadata associated with an
existing deposit. The files in the deposit remain unchanged, and the existing
DOI is preserved.

The command has one required argument: the path to the `.zenodo.toml` file. If
no path is provided, it defaults to `.zenodo.toml` in the working directory.

For example, to update the metadata of a deposit using the default
`.zenodo.toml` file, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do update
```

The following optional arguments are available:

- `--sandbox`: Update the deposit in the Zenodo sandbox environment instead of
  the main Zenodo environment. This is useful for testing changes before
  updating a real deposit.
- `--draft`: Update the deposit without publishing the changes to the record.
  This allows you to review the updated deposit before publishing it.
- `--yes`: Skip the confirmation prompt before updating. This is particularly
  useful in automated workflows, such as CI/CD pipelines.

To update a deposit in the sandbox environment without publishing the changes,
run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do update --sandbox --draft
```

By default, `update` asks for confirmation before making changes. To bypass this
prompt, for example in a continuous delivery workflow, run:

```bash {filename="Terminal"}
zen-do update --yes
```

Note that `update` requires an existing Zenodo deposit. If no deposit exists,
the command will fail. The deposit must first be published as a record (see [the
*publishing a record* guide](publishing.qmd)) before its metadata can be
updated.
